claims.text: The India Meteorological Department stated that cyclonic storm Arnab weakened into a deep depression and was expected to weaken further into a depression on Thursday morning, October 29, 2026.
Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi stated that heavy rainfall triggered by Cyclone Arnab affected at least 17 districts in southern Odisha.
Five people died in Andhra Pradesh due to Cyclone Arnab, leading Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu to announce a relief and compensation package.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu spoke to Union Home Minister Amit Shah to seek central assistance for damage to infrastructure and crops.
The Telangana government offered full support and personnel to Andhra Pradesh to assist in cyclone relief operations and power restoration.
Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts about 20 km east-northeast of Narsapur early on Wednesday before weakening to a severe cyclonic storm.
Odisha authorities shifted around 28,000 people to relief camps and relocated 2,200 pregnant women ahead of Cyclone Arnab reaching the state.
The India Meteorological Department issued a flash flood risk warning for 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh and Yanam until Thursday morning.
Five people were killed in Andhra Pradesh from tree falls and electrocution during Cyclone Arnab, with single deaths reported in Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Kakinada, Konaseema, and West Godavari.
All educational institutions in Chhattisgarh's Raipur district were ordered closed on Thursday due to forecasts of heavy rainfall and strong winds from Cyclone Arnab.
Eight people died in parts of Andhra Pradesh after severe cyclonic storm Arnab crossed the state's coast.
More than 20,000 people were evacuated in coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh prior to the arrival of Cyclone Arnab.
Cyclone Arnab crossed the coast as a very severe cyclonic storm with maximum sustained wind speeds of 125-135 kmph and gusts reaching 150 kmph.
Garividi in Vizianagaram district recorded the highest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh at 26 cm between Tuesday morning and Wednesday morning.
Three people were killed and 31 houses were damaged in Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Arnab made landfall.
Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed that 22 Indian nationals, including 14 seafarers, have been killed in the West Asia conflict zone.
Three Indian nationals were killed in Saudi Arabia in incidents linked to regional tensions in West Asia.
The Consulate General of India in Jeddah issued a travel advisory detailing expanded flight schedules by carriers such as Flynas to assist Indian nationals and Umrah pilgrims.
The United States and Israel launched military strikes on Iran on February 28, killing Iran's supreme leader and senior officials.
The United States military launched fresh attacks on Iran on July 9 after President Donald Trump declared that an interim ceasefire was over.
Three Indian seafarers—Aditya Sharma, Shivanand Chaurashiya, and Patnala Suresh—were killed on June 9 after a US strike hit the Palau-flagged oil tanker MT Settebello off Oman.
An Indian sailor was killed and six others were injured in July when Iranian missiles hit the Emirati oil tankers Mombasa and Al Bahiyah in Omani waters.
Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that India has strong relations with Israel and will work to further improve and strengthen those ties.
An estimated 64.5 lakh electors are missing from Karnataka's final electoral rolls following the Special Intensive Revision exercise, bringing the electorate down to 45,500,011.
Young adults aged 18 to 29 accounted for 59.5 percent, or 38.41 lakh, of the electors missing from Karnataka's final voter list.
The Supreme Court urged the Election Commission of India not to require nearly 4.3 million removed Delhi electors to reapply as new voters via Form 6 if they were on the 2026 rolls.
The Supreme Court stated it had not upheld the Election Commission's 'logical discrepancy' classification, which previously led to the disenfranchisement of 2.71 million people in West Bengal.
Out of approximately 14.5 million electors at the start of Delhi's Special Intensive Revision, around 4.7 million did not submit enumeration forms.
The Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls was initiated in Bihar in June 2025.
Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi formally objected 14 times in 10 months to actions taken regarding the Special Intensive Revision.
By September 1, approximately 13.37 crore names were missing from draft voter rolls across India during the Special Intensive Revision.
In a May 27 judgment, the Supreme Court ruled that the Special Intensive Revision exercise satisfied proportionality requirements and did not conflict with the Representation of the People Act.
